title: Updated report of COVID-19 vaccine safety monitoring in Japan: Booster shots and paediatric vaccinations.
ehr_evidence: reporting has been mandatory for any myocarditis/pericarditis cases within 28 days after receiving a COVID-19 vaccine, for further investigation.
summary: National pharmacovigilance safety monitoring report of COVID-19 vaccine adverse events in Japan, covering booster shots and paediatric vaccinations from December 2021 to May 2022.
key_findings: Overall reporting rates of serious adverse events for the third shot were generally lower than for the first and second shots.
Myocarditis/pericarditis reporting rates in young men with third shots tended to be higher than first shots but lower than second shots.
No confirmed causal relationship between vaccination and death was established.

In children aged 5-11 years, reporting rates for suspected myocarditis were very low with none confirmed by Brighton classification 1-3, and one confirmed pericarditis case (0.9 cases per 1 million shots).
captured_features: adverse event reports (myocarditis, pericarditis, anaphylaxis, TTS, deaths)
population: general population of Japan, including adults receiving booster doses and children aged 5-11 years
limitations: inherent reporting bias and potential underreporting of spontaneous adverse event reports
lack of individual-level clinical data beyond reported cases
reliance on mandatory reporting from healthcare professionals and marketing authorization holders
data_availability_statement: The data for this report are available to the public on the webpage (Japanese language only) of the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan ( https://www.mhlw.go.jp/stf/shingi/shingi-kousei_284075.html).
